newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND'S STARTS WEB PHONE CALLS.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND'S STARTS WEB PHONE CALLS.

text.p: Finnish state-owned telecommunications operator Telecom Finland on Tuesday said it had become the world's first post and tele operator to introduce a commercially viable Internet telephone technology service.

Voice calls over the Internet have previously been used by enthusiasts calling each other for fun, but the new service is integrated with the Internet's graphic interface area, the World Wide Web (WWW), it said in a statement.

"Telecom Finland is the first PTT to employ Internet Telephone Technology as a viable consumer and business communications solution," it quoted Elon Ganor, CEO of Tele Finland's U.S.-Israeli software partner VocalTec as saying.
"Our target is to encourage also business users to build new value-added applications based on Internet telephone services," it said.
Tele said the service would make overseas telephone calls cheaper for consumers, since much of Internet's infrastructure is publicly funded.
It would also create new opportunities, for instance in helplines and education, and Tele called the service a new step towards convergence of television and the Internet into one multimedia system.

"This is really part of the development of television and the Internet towards a full convergence," Tele quoted Jukka Mauno, project manager at Finnish commercial television channel MTV Finland, as saying.

But the Finnish news agency STT, reporting from the product launch in the western town of Tampere, said the service was slow, allowing only one-way speech signals and with a delay of up to a second and forcing long breaks between speakers.
